newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Haggie year shr seen falling.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Haggie year shr seen falling.

text.p: South African engineering group Haggie Ltd's year earnings are likely to tumble, with the company being hit by low world steel prices and losing out from the benefits of the rand's decline due to premature hedging, analysts said.
Severe competition locally would also squeeze margins and earnings, they added.

"They covered forward, so they did not get the benefit of the rand devaluation. The collapse of steel prices worldwide and tight competition locally also hit them," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
Analysts pooled by Reuters forecast earnings per share for the year ended December 31 falling to between 240.0 cents and 270.0 cents with consensus at 255.8 cents from 343.0 cents previously.
The dividend was forecast ranging between 107.3 cents and 132.0 cents with consensus at 117.8 cents down from 165.0 cents.
Legae Phahlane, engineering analyst at SBC Warburg, said the rand hedge ended in September and Haggie only enjoyed the benefits of the weaker rand for two months before its year end.
Analysts said although steel prices were weak worldwide, Haggie's entry into overseas markets would boost its revenue.
"They have a really aggressive marketing programme which will increase their share in the global market," Phahlane said.
The steel business was inccurring costs and not making up in sales as it was still in a start-up position, they said.

"Their steel wire business is still in a loss making position. The company explained it was start-up costs...CWI (Consolidated Wire Industries) has performed poorly over the last 12 months," another analyst said.
